objective.statement: Fix the brute-force bypass in the login rate limiter so that rapid spoofed requests are blocked, while legitimate users experience no added friction.
objective.success_definition: The brute-force bypass in the login rate limiter is closed; normal logins still work through the limiter; a regression test proves 101 rapid spoofed requests are blocked; no new dependencies are added, auth is not redesigned, and no CAPTCHA is introduced.

goals.statement: Fix the brute-force bypass in the login rate limiter.
acceptance: Rapid spoofed requests that previously bypassed the limiter are now blocked
A regression test issuing 101 rapid spoofed requests shows they are blocked

goals.statement: Preserve frictionless access for legitimate users; the limiter must still allow normal logins.
acceptance: Normal login attempts succeed through the rate limiter without added friction

goals.statement: Add a regression test proving 101 rapid spoofed requests are blocked.
acceptance: A regression test exists that issues 101 rapid spoofed requests
The test asserts those 101 requests are blocked and it passes

constraints.statement: No new dependencies may be added.
The fix must not add friction for legitimate users.

non_goals.statement: Adding a CAPTCHA or any similar user-facing challenge.

include: regression test for the rate limiter brute-force bypass

assumptions.statement: "Spoofed requests" refers to requests that forge the identity the rate limiter keys on (e.g., source address or equivalent identifier); the exact spoof/bypass mechanism is not specified and must be confirmed from the code.
The existing test setup can express the regression test without adding new dependencies.
The change is confined to the rate limiter module and its tests (blast radius: module); exact files are not specified.

open_questions.question: What is the exact bypass/spoof mechanism (e.g., which spoofed attribute evades the limiter)?
options: Spoofed source network identity (e.g., forwarded-for header)
Other mechanism to be determined from the code

open_questions.question: Which concrete files/modules constitute the rate limiter and its test location (i.e., the exact blast radius)?
options: Single rate limiter module plus its existing test file
Multiple modules involved in request throttling

verification.spec: Run the new regression test that issues 101 rapid spoofed requests against the login rate limiter.
verification.expected: All 101 rapid spoofed requests are blocked and the test passes.

verification.spec: Exercise normal login attempts through the rate limiter after the fix.
verification.expected: Legitimate logins succeed with no added friction.

deliverables.description: Fix to the login rate limiter that closes the brute-force bypass.
Regression test proving 101 rapid spoofed requests are blocked.

factors: Change touches security-sensitive login throttling; an incorrect fix could leave the bypass open or lock out legitimate users
The exact spoof/bypass mechanism is not specified in the task and must be confirmed from the code
Constraints (no new dependencies, no auth redesign, no CAPTCHA) narrow the solution space
